metadata.title: Filmtone
metadata.description: A real-time color grading tool in the browser. Drop images or videos, then adjust exposure, contrast, and LUT with GPU fragment shaders.
metadata.ogDescription: Drop an image or video and grade it in real-time. Exposure, contrast, LUT, and film presets powered by WebGL2 GPU shaders.

share.postText: Try this grade in Filmtone — browser color grading

browser.hint: Keeps your look on this device only. Tap Save when you want to keep the current grade. Opening this page without a share link loads the last save automatically.
browser.feedbackError: Could not read or write. Check private mode or storage limits.

smartLook.sectionTitle: Match colors to a sample (AI, beta)
smartLook.consentSummary: Supporters only. We send two small images—your edit and one sample—and AI suggests how to align color.
smartLook.consentHint: We send (1) the graded preview on screen and (2) one sample image you pick, resized, through our server to an AI provider. The reply may be slider hints or, depending on settings, a preview image. Not used to train models. See our privacy policy for subprocessors and retention.
smartLook.consentInfoAria: What is sent and privacy details
smartLook.consentLabel: I agree to send both images
smartLook.referenceSummary: Pick one sample photo from disk with the look you want.
smartLook.referenceTooltip: Use a different file from what’s on the canvas—the canvas preview is sent automatically. JPEG, PNG, or WebP.
smartLook.errorReferenceRead: Couldn’t read that file. Try JPEG, PNG, or WebP.
smartLook.errorGeneric: Something went wrong. Adjust with sliders or try again later.
smartLook.errorRateLimit: You’ve hit today’s limit. Try tomorrow or use sliders.
smartLook.errorProvider: Couldn’t reach the service. Try again later or use sliders.
smartLook.errorInvalidResponse: Couldn’t read the result. Try a different sample or use sliders.

smartLook.supporterOnly: This is for supporters. Support via Stripe in the footer to unlock.

effects.lensSoftnessHint: Softens detail toward the frame edges, like mild lens falloff—isotropic blur, not a motion radial or zoom blur.

shortcuts.presetSlider: Blend film preset vs neutral (when preset active)

controls.bloomToggleHint: Soft glow that spreads from bright areas (bloom).
controls.bloomThresholdHint: Only pixels brighter than this level contribute strongly to the glow.
controls.halationToggleHint: Colored glow around very bright edges (halation).
controls.artifactsSectionHint: Grain, vignette, glow, halation, and related film-look controls.
controls.sourceTrimSectionHint: Adjust the imported image before the film look—exposure, color, highlights, and shadows.
controls.compressionToggleHint: Turn highlight compression on or off. Pushing it too far can break the image, so use it only when needed.
controls.compressionHint: Softens bright tones with a film-style shoulder curve. Push it too far and the image can go flat, so keep it in a safe range.
controls.compressionRangeHint: Controls how far that softness spreads across the tonal range. Wider values can make the effect feel stronger, so the slider is capped conservatively.
controls.printContrastHint: Adds contrast in the print-style stage—separate from the main Contrast slider in the grading stack.
controls.rgbShiftToggleHint: Turn chromatic aberration on or off. It can break the image if pushed too far, so use it only when needed.
controls.grainRadialMixHint: Near 0: even grain. Near 1: stronger toward frame edges (not chromatic aberration). At 1 matches the previous default.

batch.tipExportTabIntro: Photos in a folder can be saved in bulk to another folder with your Filmtone look. You can also export one video as MP4 with the same look. After adjusting sliders on Edit, use “Send grade to Export” (bottom right) to copy values here. LUTs are separate (e.g. load JSON).
batch.tipJobImages: Every .jpg / .jpeg / .png in the chosen folder gets this look, saved as JPEG or PNG to another folder.
batch.tipJobVideoWebGlOnly: Exports one video as MP4 with a look close to the Edit tab, grading frame by frame. Long clips can take a while to finish. ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH.
batch.tipSourcesImagesFolder: Only .jpg / .jpeg / .png in that folder (not subfolders by default in UI copy). Not for video conversion.
batch.tipSourcesVideoFile: Import limit: up to 4K and max {maxSec}s. ffmpeg and ffprobe must be on PATH.
batch.tipLookJsonDetails: Use when passing or saving a full look (including LUT) as a file. Usually “Send grade to Export” or preset is enough.
batch.tipApplyEditGradeToBatch: Copies Edit sliders here (same as “Send grade to Export”). After a preset change, preset values stay until you sync. LUT: use “Advanced: Grade JSON”.
batch.tipFilenameSuffix: Inserted before the extension. Example: -graded → IMG0001-graded.jpg. Empty = no suffix. Use a different folder than sources to avoid overwriting.
batch.tipVideoOutputNaming: Output file name is original stem + -graded.mp4. Max output FHD · {fps} fps.
batch.tipKeyboardShortcuts: ⌘1 / ⌘2 / ⌘3 (Ctrl on Windows) switch Edit, Photos, and Video. On Photos, ⌘↵ runs batch export; on Video, ⌘↵ exports the clip. ⇧⌘↵ retries failed items (Photos only). ⇧⌘Y resumes (Photos only). Esc cancels.
batch.tipDesktopPrefsPersist: Input/output folders become defaults next time (existing paths). Window position and size are saved on quit.
batch.tipResumeSession: Continue with saved I/O and look for remaining frames only. Discard removes the record only — already exported files stay on disk.
